title: Locker gold went 'missing', but an undated photo wasn't proof

slides.head: Locker gold went 'missing', but an undated photo wasn't proof
What happened
slides.body: The holders said they kept about 200 g of gold in 2015; in 2016 eight coins, two bars and some melted gold were found missing.

slides.head: Why it matters
slides.body: The bank said a locker needs two keys, only holders know its contents, and there was no sign of the locker being forced.

slides.head: gold claimed missing
slides.body: The deciding factor: their only proof was a photo with no date or signature.

slides.head: Dig deeper
slides.body: Opening the locker needs two keys, one with the customer and one with the bank.

slides.head: What to watch
slides.body: The pending protest petition against the police's 'undetectable' closure of the theft case. Ask: What proof should locker holders keep of what's inside?

captions.instagram:
Locker gold went 'missing', but an undated photo wasn't proof

The Telangana State Consumer Commission upheld a district order dismissing a claim that gold coins, bars and melted gold went missing from a jointly held SBI locker in Hyderabad.

Why it matters: The bank said a locker needs two keys, only holders know its contents, and there was no sign of the locker being forced.

Source: Times of India. Image: Times of India
